concepts.name: NDA effective date
justifications: The agreement expressly sets the Effective Date as 1 February 2027 and states that effectiveness was deferred to that date, although both parties signed on 29 January 2027.

concepts.name: NDA permitted purpose
predicted: evaluating a possible minority investment by talus ventures ab in fjordsignal as's marine sensor business under project glassfinch.
gold: evaluating a possible minority investment by the recipient in the discloser's marine sensor business under project glassfinch.
values: Evaluating a possible minority investment by Talus Ventures AB in FjordSignal AS's marine sensor business under Project Glassfinch.
justifications: The agreement defines this as the sole Permitted Purpose.

concepts.name: NDA disclosure window end
justifications: The termination notice was delivered on 24 November 2027 and specifies an effective closing date of 30 November 2027, earlier than the ordinary end date.

concepts.name: NDA contractual forum
justifications: The agreement expressly designates the courts of Oslo as the parties’ contractual forum.

concepts.name: NDA signatory entities
justifications: FjordSignal AS is identified as registered in Norway and as the Discloser.
Talus Ventures AB is identified as registered in Sweden and as the Recipient.

concepts.name: Protected assets at the April snapshot
justifications: LUMEN’s nonpublic selection, ordering, and combined settings remain protected despite its public components, and SHORE’s nonpublic additions mean the complete package is not wholly excluded. CEDAR had not been publicly released by the snapshot, while BASALT’s public posting resulted from a breach and does not establish the public-information exclusion.

concepts.name: ORACLE timely confirmation deadline
justifications: Counting five Business Days after the 25 March 2027 oral disclosure, while excluding the specified non-Business Days, makes 5 April the final day for timely confirmation.

concepts.name: ORACLE protection timeline
predicted: protection is not continuous. oracle was provisionally protected from its oral disclosure on 25 march 2027 until the five-business-day confirmation deadline of 5 april 2027 at 17:00 utc. although the confirmation was sent on 5 april at 16:58, it was delivered to the recipient mailbox on 6 april at 09:05, after the deadline, so protection lapsed at the deadline. the gap ended when the recipient expressly accepted the late confirmation on 8 april at 10:00 utc, restoring protection prospectively from that time; sending the confirmation did not make it timely.
gold: oracle is provisionally protected from the 25 march oral disclosure until 5 april 2027 at 17:00 utc. confirmation sent before that deadline arrived late on 6 april at 09:05, so protection lapses after the deadline. it resumes prospectively when the recipient expressly accepts on 8 april at 10:00 utc; the gap is not cured retroactively.
values: Protection is not continuous. ORACLE was provisionally protected from its oral disclosure on 25 March 2027 until the five-Business-Day confirmation deadline of 5 April 2027 at 17:00 UTC. Although the confirmation was sent on 5 April at 16:58, it was delivered to the recipient mailbox on 6 April at 09:05, after the deadline, so protection lapsed at the deadline. The gap ended when the Recipient expressly accepted the late confirmation on 8 April at 10:00 UTC, restoring protection prospectively from that time; sending the confirmation did not make it timely.
justifications: The oral disclosure was identified as confidential, but the required written confirmation was delivered after the five-Business-Day deadline. The agreement makes delivery, not sending, controlling and states that late acceptance restores protection only prospectively.

concepts.name: Entire SHORE package excluded by prior possession
justifications: The prior repository contains only the smaller module incorporated into the package; there is no evidence of prior possession of the new non-public branching map, thresholds, or complete package.

concepts.name: CEDAR end of protection
justifications: The entire schedule was independently and lawfully released to the unrestricted public on this date, establishing the public-information exclusion for the complete asset. Protection therefore ended then, rather than at the ordinary duration deadline.

concepts.name: People permitted LUMEN access at the September snapshot
justifications: Elin and Marek meet the applicable employee, undertaking, security-check, and named-approval requirements; Talus Research AB qualifies as an Affiliate with 52% of the votes at the snapshot. Oskar qualifies as a professional legal adviser relying on his enforceable duty of confidence; Nora lacks an effective undertaking, Pia lacks signed competitor consent, and Ravi is employed by an entity that does not meet the voting-control test.

concepts.name: Talus Research qualifying voting percentage
justifications: The Recipient’s 48% of directly held votes and a disjoint 4% covered by a presently effective, irrevocable proxy count at the access snapshot, totaling 52%.

concepts.name: Marek earliest authorised LUMEN access
justifications: Talus Research qualifies as an Affiliate at the relevant time because the Recipient holds 48% of votes and has an effective irrevocable proxy over a disjoint 4%. Marek's undertaking and security check were effective by 10 September, but his named clean-room approval did not become effective until 14 September, when all stated access requirements were met.

concepts.name: Executed competitor consent date for Pia
Q-27 notice deadline date
justifications: Because notice was initially prohibited, the deadline is the earlier of six continuous hours after the prohibition was lifted and the production time. Six hours after the prohibition was lifted at 11:20 on 5 July 2027 is 17:20 that day, earlier than the production time.

concepts.name: Q-27 notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Because notice was initially prohibited, the deadline was the earlier of six continuous hours after the prohibition was lifted (17:20 on 5 July) and the production time. The notice arrived at 17:55, 35 minutes after that deadline; actual arrival controls.

concepts.name: Q-27 permitted production units
justifications: The final binding narrowing order requires all of P1 and only non-privileged subsection P3A; P3B is privileged and P2 and P4 were withdrawn.

concepts.name: WORK-1 deletion deadline
justifications: The return request was delivered on 22 November, earlier than the termination trigger, so the ten-Business-Day period began on the next eligible day. WORK-1 is an active copy and restoration does not restart its deadline; no binding preservation order covers it.

concepts.name: BK-1 deletion deadline
justifications: The return request received on 22 November triggered the deletion period before the later effective termination. BK-1 may remain only until the earlier of its scheduled 30 December overwrite and 45 calendar days after that trigger; the overwrite comes first, and restoring WORK-1 does not reset either clock.

concepts.name: Artifacts permitted retention at the December snapshot
justifications: ARCH-1 qualifies as the segregated counsel-held archival copy, BK-1 may remain until its scheduled overwrite, and HOLD-1 is covered by a binding preservation order still in force at the snapshot. WORK-1 is an overdue active copy, and NOTE-1 has no applicable retention exception.

concepts.name: NOTE-1 model training permitted as residual knowledge
justifications: NOTE-1 consists of deliberately recorded parameter values and reconstruction notes, which are excluded from the residual-knowledge permission. Training a model with Confidential Information is prohibited without a separate signed licence, and none covers this use.
